<reason>B won by distinguishing scientific value from authority to compel research, while explicitly accepting that return can sacrifice irreplaceable knowledge. A made that loss vivid but did not adequately establish who should override legitimate recipients or why institutions should determine future descendants’ interests. B answered the identification challenge directly and showed that future generations inherit community autonomy as well as information. A’s final irreversibility comparison sharpened its case, but limiting an unwanted study did not resolve those objections.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s strongest rebuttal granted one bounded study and guaranteed return, then explained that a deadline limits the override without justifying it. This directly undermined A’s proposed compromise rather than relying solely on the risk of endless delay.</best_rebuttal>
